content: Evidence regarding the optimal frequency of blood glucose monitoring (BGM) for individuals with diabetes who are using only basal insulin or noninsulin injectable therapies remains limited. Current research does not provide clear guidance on how often these individuals should perform BGM. While BGM, when combined with appropriate education, has been associated with modest reductions in A1C levels, its effectiveness is significantly enhanced when integrated into a structured self-management program. Findings from a year-long study indicate that individuals who had not previously used insulin and who consistently performed BGM while receiving structured feedback experienced a reduction in A1C levels that was 0.3% greater than those who engaged in BGM without structured guidance. This highlights the importance of structured feedback in achieving better glycemic control.
